title: Ostwald's Dilution Law and Degree of Dissociation

references.label: NCERT Chemistry Part I, Class 11 — Equilibrium

expression: Ka = Cα²/(1−α)  ;  for small α: α ≈ √(Ka/C)
explanation: Ostwald's dilution law relates a weak electrolyte's dissociation constant Ka to its degree of dissociation α (fraction of molecules ionised) and concentration C. For weak electrolytes with small α (α << 1), the approximation α ≈ √(Ka/C) shows degree of dissociation INCREASES as concentration DECREASES (i.e., dissociation increases on dilution) — consistent with Le Chatelier's principle, since dilution favours the side producing more particles (more ions).

variables.meaning: Initial (analytical) concentration of the weak electrolyte

workedExample.scenario: A weak acid with Ka = 1.8×10⁻⁵ at concentration 0.1 mol/L.

commonMistakes: Assuming degree of dissociation stays constant regardless of concentration — for a weak electrolyte, α actually INCREASES as the solution is diluted (concentration decreases), per Ostwald's dilution law.

Applying the simplified approximation (α ≈ √(Ka/C)) when α is NOT small — the approximation (1−α ≈ 1) breaks down for more strongly dissociating weak electrolytes or very dilute solutions, requiring the full quadratic form instead.
genZNote: Dilute a weak acid enough, and it dissociates more — Ostwald's law rewards giving it more room to ionise.
